translation_notes: SH is a run-time parameter here (rdflib.Namespace passed in by the caller), not a fixed constant, so every predicate is written as an interpolated `{SH.inversePath}` etc. rather than a `sh:` prefix declaration -- a `@prefix sh: <...>` would silently hard-code the namespace the original leaves open to the caller.

The region's `strata` lists both trav_single_value (line 426, `graph.value(path_node, SH.inversePath)`) and trav_existence (line 435, `graph.value(path_node, rdflib.RDF.first) is not None`); both sites got their own most-specific construction -- `.first()` and `bool(m{ })` respectively -- rather than degrading the existence check to `.first() is not None` just because the region lives under trav_single_value.

optimization_notes: Both sides: the two-step sequence test (`steps = _rdf_list(...)`, then `len(steps) == 2 and isinstance(steps[0], URIRef) and steps[1] == RDF.type`, then `_local(steps[0])`) becomes one `match _rdf_list(...)` with `case [rdflib.URIRef() as assoc, rdflib.RDF.type]:` -- same length test, same isinstance, same equality, no `steps` variable.

Not compressed: every `is not None` test stays (the fixture has a falsy Literal("") and Literal(0) inverse that a truthiness test would drop); the direct inverse read is not merged into the alternative-path loop, which would read the alternative list before returning on a direct inverse.
